analysis:
This batch contains only documentation: a new changelog fragment (changelog.d/cluster-pair-serving-epoch.md, lines 1-16) and docs/architecture/inference.md (date bump at line 3, new paragraph at head lines 59-72). No source code is supplied, so the behavior itself is unverified here. The text describes a deadlock fix in the two-Mac pair's distributed CBv2 engine. Request stream onTermination and admission cancellation now hop onto the engine queue without waiting (onQueueWithoutWaiting), and the retirement task no longer blocks a cooperative thread. It also describes the leader releasing a committed start when its session ends, while the release receipt still waits, bounded, for the slot to retire. The text states that a pair still never serves two slots at once.

Security relevance is availability (a stuck slot retirement or a refused start), which is not tied to any retained threat. The relevant boundaries are TB-007 and the cluster serving lifecycle, and no cluster-specific threat is defined in the supplied index. Retirement ordering also touches decrypted-prompt and KV residency (T-028) and the one-slot-at-a-time invariant.

Two questions for integration or the code PRs. First, early release of the committed-start record, before the old slot fully retires, could briefly allow overlap of old and new slot state. The docs say the receipt still waits, bounded, for retirement, but this cannot be verified here. Second, the "bounded" wait on the release receipt is unspecified, and its expiry behavior is unknown. These are documented claims in the supplied evidence, not demonstrated regressions. The docs change no controls, and no finding qualifies. Review of the actual DistributedCBv2Engine.swift and DistributedCBv2Engine+Admission.swift changes is advisable if they are in a separate batch.
